readings.title: Following the Covenant Guarantee
readings.subtitle: Preparing for Wonders
readings.text:
[Joshua 3:1] And Yehoshua rose early in the morning, and they set out from Shittim and came to the Yardên, he and all the children of Yisra’ěl, and stayed there before they passed over.
[2] And it came to be, after three days, that the officers went into the midst of the camp,
[3] and they commanded <dn>את</dn> the people, saying, “When you see <dn>את</dn> the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and the priests, the Lěvites, bearing it, then you shall set out from your place and follow it.
[4] “Only, keep a distance between you and it, about two thousand cubits by measure. Do not come near it, so that you know <dn>את</dn> which way to go, for you have not passed over this way before.”
[5] And Yehoshua said to the people, “Set yourselves apart, for tomorrow <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is doing wonders in your midst.”
[6] And Yehoshua spoke to the priests, saying, “Take up <dn>את</dn> the ark of the covenant and pass over before the people.” So they took up <dn>את</dn> the ark of the covenant and went before the people.

readings.subsection: The Master of All the Earth
readings.title: Establishing Yehoshua's Authority
readings.subtitle: The Waters Commanded to Stand
readings.text:
[7] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yehoshua, <dq>“This day <dn>I</dn> begin to make you great before the eyes of all Yisra’ěl, so that they know that <dn>I</dn> am with <dn>את</dn> you as <dn>I</dn> was with <dn>את</dn> Mosheh.</dq>
[8] <dq>“And you, command <dn>את</dn> the priests who bear the ark of the covenant, saying, ‘When you come to the edge of the water of the Yardên, stand in the Yardên.’ ”</dq>
[9] And Yehoshua said to the children of Yisra’ěl, “Come near, and hear <dn>את</dn> the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.”
[10] And Yehoshua said, “By this you shall know that the living <dn>Ěl</dn> is in your midst, and that <dn>He</dn> is certainly driving out from before you <dn>את</dn> the Kenaʽanites and <dn>את</dn> the Ḥittites and <dn>את</dn> the Ḥivvites and <dn>את</dn> the Perizzites and <dn>את</dn> the Girgashites and <dn>את</dn> the Amorites and <dn>את</dn> the Yeḇusites:
[11] “See, the ark of the covenant of the Master of all the earth is passing over before you into the Yardên.
[12] “And now, take for yourselves twelve men from the tribes of Yisra’ěl, one man from every tribe.
[13] “And it shall be, as soon as the soles of the feet of the priests who bear the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the Master of all the earth, come to rest in the waters of the Yardên, that the waters of the Yardên are cut off, the waters that come down from upstream, and stand as a heap.”

readings.title: The Yardên Cut Off
readings.subtitle: Yisra’ěl Passes on Dry Ground
readings.text:
[14] And it came to be, when the people set out from their tents to pass over <dn>את</dn> the Yardên, with the priests bearing the ark of the covenant before the people,
[15] and as those bearing the ark came to the Yardên, and the feet of the priests bearing the ark dipped in the edge of the water – now the Yardên overflows all its banks during all the time of harvest –
[16] that the waters which came down from upstream stood still, and rose in a heap very far away at Aḏam, the city that is beside Tsarethan. And the waters going down into the Sea of the Araḇah, the Salt Sea, were completely cut off. And the people passed over opposite Yeriḥo.
[17] And the priests bearing the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> stood firm on dry ground in the midst of the Yardên. And all Yisra’ěl passed over on dry ground, until all the nation had completely passed over <dn>את</dn> the Yardên.

readings.title: Twelve Stones from the Riverbed
readings.subtitle: A Sign for the Next Generation
readings.text:
[Joshua 4:1] And it came to be, when the entire nation had completely passed over <dn>את</dn> the Yardên, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Yehoshua, saying,
[2] <dq>“Take for yourselves twelve men from the people, one man from every tribe,</dq>
[3] <dq>and command <dn>את</dn> them, saying, ‘Take for yourselves twelve stones from here, out of the midst of the Yardên, from the place where the priests’ feet stood firm. And you shall bring them with <dn>את</dn> you and leave them in the camp in which you spend the night.’ ”</dq>
[4] And Yehoshua called the twelve men whom he had appointed from the children of Yisra’ěl, one man from every tribe,
[5] and Yehoshua said to them, “Pass over before the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> into the midst of the Yardên, and each one of you take up a stone on his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Yisra’ěl,
[6] so that this shall be a sign in your midst when your children ask in time to come, saying, ‘What do these stones mean to you?’
[7] “Then you shall answer them that the waters of the Yardên were cut off before the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. When it passed over the Yardên, the waters of the Yardên were cut off. And these stones shall be for a remembrance to the children of Yisra’ěl forever.”
[8] And the children of Yisra’ěl did so, as Yehoshua commanded, and took up twelve stones from the midst of the Yardên, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had spoken to Yehoshua, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Yisra’ěl, and took them over with them to their camp, and laid them down there.
[9] Yehoshua also set up twelve stones in the midst of the Yardên, in the place where the feet of the priests who bore the ark of the covenant stood. And they are there to this day.

readings.title: The Ark Ascends from the Yardên
readings.subtitle: The Waters Return to Their Place
readings.text:
[10] And the priests who bore the ark stood in the midst of the Yardên until every matter was finished that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded <dn>את</dn> Yehoshua to speak to the people, according to all that Mosheh had commanded <dn>את</dn> Yehoshua. And the people hastened and passed over.
[11] And it came to be, when all the people had completely passed over, that the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the priests passed over in the presence of the people.
[12] And the sons of Re’uḇěn, and the sons of Gaḏ, and half the tribe of Menashsheh passed over in fives before the children of Yisra’ěl, as Mosheh had spoken to them.
[13] About forty thousand armed ones of the army passed over before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for battle, to the desert plains of Yeriḥo.
[14] On that day <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made <dn>את</dn> Yehoshua great before the eyes of all Yisra’ěl. And they feared <dn>את</dn> him, as they had feared <dn>את</dn> Mosheh, all the days of his life.
[15] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Yehoshua, saying,
[16] <dq>"Command <dn>את</dn> the priests who bear the ark of the Witness, and let them come up from the Yardên.”</dq>
[17] And Yehoshua commanded <dn>את</dn> the priests, saying, “Come up from the Yardên.”
[18] And it came to be, when the priests who bore the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had come from the midst of the Yardên, and the soles of the priests’ feet touched the dry land, that the waters of the Yardên returned to their place and flowed over all its banks as before.

readings.title: The Memorial Stones Set Up
readings.subtitle: The Hearts of the Adversaries Melt
readings.text:
[19] And the people came up from the Yardên on the tenth day of the first new moon, and they camped in Gilgal on the east border of Yeriḥo.
[20] And <dn>את</dn> those twelve stones which they took out of the Yardên, Yehoshua set up in Gilgal.
[21] And he said to the children of Yisra’ěl, saying, “When your children ask <dn>את</dn> their fathers in time to come, saying, ‘What are these stones?’
[22] then you shall let <dn>את</dn> your children know, saying, ‘Yisra’ěl passed over <dn>את</dn> this Yardên on dry land,’
[23] for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> dried up <dn>את</dn> the waters of the Yardên before you until you had passed over, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> did to the Sea of Reeds, which <dn>He</dn> dried up before us until we had passed over,
[24] so that all the peoples of the earth shall know <dn>את</dn> the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that it is strong, so that you shall fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> forever.”
[Joshua 5:1] And it came to be, when all the sovereigns of the Amorites who were beyond the Yardên westward, and all the sovereigns of the Kenaʽanites who were by the sea, heard that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had dried up <dn>את</dn> the waters of the Yardên from before the children of Yisra’ěl until we had passed over, that their heart melted. And there was no spirit in them any longer, because of the children of Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: Circumcision at Gilgal
readings.subtitle: The Reproach of Mitsrayim Rolled Away
readings.text:
[Joshua 5:2] At that time <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yehoshua, <dq>“Make knives of flint for yourself, and circumcise <dn>את</dn> the sons of Yisra’ěl again the second time.”</dq>
[3] So Yehoshua made knives of flint for himself, and circumcised <dn>את</dn> the sons of Yisra’ěl at the Hill of Foreskins.
[4] And this is why Yehoshua circumcised them: All the people who came out of Mitsrayim who were males, all the men of battle, had died in the wilderness on the way, after they had come out of Mitsrayim.
[5] For all the people who came out had been circumcised, but all the people who were born in the wilderness on the way as they came out of Mitsrayim had not been circumcised.
[6] For the children of Yisra’ěl walked forty years in the wilderness, till all the nation – the men of battle who came out of Mitsrayim – were consumed, because they did not obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> swore not to show them <dn>את</dn> the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had sworn to their fathers that <dn>He</dn> would give us, “a land flowing with milk and honey.”
[7] And Yehoshua circumcised <dn>את</dn> their sons whom <dn>He</dn> raised up in their place; for they were uncircumcised, because they had not been circumcised on the way.
[8] And it came to be, when they had completed circumcising all the nation, that they stayed in their places in the camp till they were healed.
[9] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yehoshua, <dq>“Today <dn>I</dn> have rolled away <dn>את</dn> the reproach of Mitsrayim from you.”</dq> So the name of the place is called Gilgal to this day.

readings.title: Keeping the Pěsaḥ
readings.subtitle: The Manna Ceases and Provision Shifts
readings.text:
[10] And the children of Yisra’ěl camped in Gilgal, and performed <dn>את</dn> the Pěsaḥ on the fourteenth day of the new moon at evening on the desert plains of Yeriḥo.
[11] And they ate of the stored grain of the land on the morrow after the Pěsaḥ, unleavened bread and roasted grain on this same day.
[12] And the manna ceased on the day after they had eaten the stored grain of the land. And the children of Yisra’ěl no longer had manna, but they ate the food of the land of Kenaʽan that year.

readings.title: The Captain of YeHoVaH's Host
readings.subtitle: Holy Ground Before Yeriḥo
readings.text:
[13] And it came to be, when Yehoshua was by Yeriḥo, that he lifted his eyes and looked and saw a Man standing opposite him with <dn>His</dn> sword drawn in <dn>His</dn> hand. And Yehoshua went to <dn>Him</dn> and said to <dn>Him</dn>, “Are You for us or for our adversaries?”
[14] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“No, for <dn>I</dn> have now come as Captain of the host of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq> And Yehoshua fell on his face to the earth and did obeisance, and said to <dn>Him</dn>, “What is my Master saying to <dn>His</dn> servant?”
[15] And the Captain of the host of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yehoshua, <dq>“Take your sandal off your foot, for the place where you stand is set-apart.”</dq> And Yehoshua did so.

readings.title: The Divine Strategy Issued
readings.subtitle: The Shopharot of the Yoḇelim
readings.text:
[Joshua 6:1] And Yeriḥo was shut up tight because of the presence of the sons of Yisra’ěl – none going out, and none coming in.
[2] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Yehoshua, <dq>“See! <dn>I</dn> have given <dn>את</dn> Yeriḥo and <dn>את</dn> its sovereign, mighty brave men, into your hand.</dq>
[3] <dq>“And you shall go around <dn>את</dn> the city, all the men of battle going around <dn>את</dn> the city once. Do this for six days.</dq>
[4] <dq>“And let seven priests bear seven shopharot of the yoḇelim before the ark, and on the seventh day go around <dn>את</dn> the city seven times while the priests blow with the shopharot.</dq>
[5] <dq>“And it shall be, when they make a long blast with the horn of a yoḇel, and when you hear <dn>את</dn> the voice of the shophar, that all the people shout with a great sound. And the wall of the city shall fall down flat, and the people shall go up every man straight before him.”</dq>

readings.title: Six Days of Silent Marching
readings.subtitle: The Ark Circles the City
readings.text:
[6] And Yehoshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, “Take up <dn>את</dn> the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests bear seven shopharot of yoḇelim before the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”
[7] And he said to the people, “Pass over, and go around <dn>את</dn> the city, and let him who is armed pass over before the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”
[8] And it came to be, when Yehoshua had spoken to the people, that the seven priests bearing the seven shopharot of the yoḇelim before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> passed over and blew with the shopharot, and the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> went after them.
[9] And the armed men went before the priests who blew the shopharot, and the rear guard came after the ark, going on and blowing with the shopharot.
[10] But Yehoshua had commanded <dn>את</dn> the people, saying, “Do not make a sound or cause <dn>את</dn> your voice to be heard, nor let any word come out of your mouth, until the day I say to you, ‘Shout!’ Then you shall shout.”
[11] And the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> went around <dn>את</dn> the city, going around once. And they came into the camp and stayed in the camp.
[12] And Yehoshua rose early in the morning, and the priests took up <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[13] And seven priests bearing seven shopharot of the yoḇelim before the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> were walking, going on, and they blew with the shopharot, and the armed men went before them. But the rear guard came after the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, going on, and blowing with the shopharot.
[14] And the second day they went around <dn>את</dn> the city once and returned to the camp. Thus they did six days.

readings.title: The Great Shout and the Falling Walls
readings.subtitle: Yeriḥo Placed Under the Ban
readings.text:
[15] And it came to be on the seventh day that they rose early, about the dawning of the day, and went around <dn>את</dn> the city seven times in this way. Only on that day they went around <dn>את</dn> the city seven times.
[16] And it came to be at the seventh time, when the priests blew with the shopharot, that Yehoshua said to the people, “Shout, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has given you <dn>את</dn> the city!
[17] “And the city shall be put under the ban, it and all that is in it belongs to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Only Raḥaḇ the whore is to live, she and all who are with her in the house, because she hid <dn>את</dn> the messengers that we sent.
[18] “And you, by all means guard yourselves from that which is under the ban, lest you come under the ban when you take of that which is under the ban, and make <dn>את</dn> the camp of Yisra’ěl a curse, and shall trouble it.
[19] “But all the silver and gold, and vessels of bronze and iron, are set-apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, they go into the treasury of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”
[20] And the people shouted when the priests blew the shopharot. And it came to be when the people heard <dn>את</dn> the voice of the shophar, and the people shouted with a great shout, that the wall fell down flat. And the people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they captured <dn>את</dn> the city.
[21] And they put under the ban <dn>את</dn> all that was in the city, both man and woman, young and old, and ox and sheep and donkey, with the edge of the sword.

readings.title: Raḥaḇ the Whore Rescued
readings.subtitle: A Perpetual Curse Placed on Yeriḥo
readings.text:
[22] And to the two men who had spied out <dn>את</dn> the land Yehoshua said, “Go into the house of the woman, the whore, and from there bring out <dn>את</dn> the woman and <dn>את</dn> all that she has, as you swore to her.”
[23] And the young men, the spies, went in and brought out <dn>את</dn> Raḥaḇ, and <dn>את</dn> her father, and <dn>את</dn> her mother, and <dn>את</dn> her brothers, and <dn>את</dn> all that she had. So they brought out <dn>את</dn> all her relatives and set them outside the camp of Yisra’ěl.
[24] And they burned <dn>את</dn> the city and <dn>את</dn> all that was in it with fire. Only the silver and gold, and the vessels of bronze and of iron, they put into the treasury of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[25] However, Yehoshua kept alive <dn>את</dn> Raḥaḇ the whore, and <dn>את</dn> her father’s household, and <dn>את</dn> all that she had. And she dwelt in the midst of Yisra’ěl to this day, because she hid <dn>את</dn> the messengers whom Yehoshua sent to spy out <dn>את</dn> Yeriḥo.
[26] And Yehoshua warned them at that time, saying, “Cursed is the man before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who rises up and builds <dn>את</dn> this city <dn>את</dn> Yeriḥo – he lays its foundation with his first-born, and with his youngest he sets up its gates.”
[27] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was with <dn>את</dn> Yehoshua, and a report about him was in all the land.
